QUOTE: `ExternalBridge::start` (`external_bridge.cpp:796`) | `accept_loop` ... Each client gets its own `ClientThread`, held in `client_threads_` ... `ExternalBridge::accept_loop` (`:945`) | per-client `serve_client`
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says start spawns the accept_loop thread, and accept_loop spawns a per-client serve_client thread for each accepted connection. That is the two-level structure.
